plan: Given my private value of $13, I should bid strategically to maximize profit. To ensure profit, my bid should be below my value. Bidding slightly lower than my value, say $12, allows me to win if others value it less, while ensuring I don't overpay. This bid maximizes potential profit by keeping costs low if I win.

Given my value of $15, I aim to maximize profit while minimizing risk. Bidding above $15 is unwise as it risks overpaying. A bid slightly below $15, such as $14, might win if others undervalue the item. This ensures I do not pay more than my perceived value, aligning with long-term profit maximization.

Given my private value of $47, I aim to bid close to it to maximize my profit if I win. Since the prize value is drawn independently each round, I will bid slightly lower to ensure a positive profit margin. To balance winning chances and potential profit, I will bid $46. This ensures that if I win, I gain significant value while minimizing the risk of overpaying, considering the third-highest bid will be lower than $46.
